content.text: {"predictors": [{"name": "Inventory Growth Divergence", "construction": "For each firm, compute year-over-year growth in inventories (Compustat item INVT) minus year-over-year growth in sales (item SALE), measured at fiscal year end and matched to returns with a 6-month lag. Rank cross-sectionally.", "rationale": "Inventories accumulating faster than sales signal overproduction and weak future demand, foreshadowing markdowns and earnings disappointments.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (inventory growth below sales growth)"}, {"name": "Depreciation-to-CapEx Aging", "construction": "Compute the ratio of accumulated depreciation (Compustat item DPACT) to gross PP&E (item PPEGT), and separately depreciation expense (item DP) to capital expenditures (item CAPX). Average the two into an asset-aging score, updated annually with a 6-month reporting lag.", "rationale": "Firms with old, underinvested asset bases face lower reinvestment needs and higher free-cash-flow yields, and the market underprices this hidden efficiency.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (older asset base, low reinvestment)"}, {"name": "Selling-Expense Operating Leverage", "construction": "Compute SG&A expense (Compustat item XSGA) scaled by sales (item SALE), then take the change in this ratio versus the prior fiscal year. Combine with total-asset turnover (SALE/AT). Rank on the interaction of high SG&A intensity and improving turnover, lagged 6 months.", "rationale": "High fixed selling-cost bases create operating leverage; when turnover improves, earnings rise disproportionately, a mispriced nonlinearity.", "higher_returns_for": "high SG&A intensity combined with improving asset turnover"}, {"name": "Dividend Initiation Persistence Gap", "construction": "Using CRSP distribution codes, identify firms that raised their regular cash dividend in each of the prior three fiscal years. Score = number of consecutive annual increases. Match to monthly returns.", "rationale": "A multi-year record of dividend increases signals durable cash-flow quality that investors extrapolate too weakly, leaving positive drift.", "higher_returns_for": "high values (longer streak of consecutive dividend increases)"}, {"name": "Share-Count Stability", "construction": "Compute the standard deviation of month-end shares outstanding (CRSP SHROUT) over the trailing 36 months, scaled by mean shares. Lower dispersion indicates absence of dilution and equity issuance.", "rationale": "Firms that neither dilute nor repeatedly issue equity tend to be self-financing and undervalued; volatile share counts flag financing distress or empire-building.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (stable share count)"}, {"name": "Accrual-Adjusted Earnings Momentum", "construction": "Compute standardized unexpected earnings (SUE) from Compustat quarterly EPS (item EPSPXQ) using a seasonal-random-walk expectation, then subtract the current-quarter total accruals scaled by assets (change in non-cash working capital minus depreciation, from the funds-flow statement). Rank on the cash-based SUE.", "rationale": "Earnings surprises backed by cash rather than accruals are more persistent, so cash-adjusted momentum predicts stronger post-announcement drift.", "higher_returns_for": "high cash-based earnings surprise"}, {"name": "Trading-Volume Trend Reversal", "construction": "For each stock compute average daily dollar volume (CRSP price times volume) in the most recent month divided by average daily dollar volume over the trailing 12 months. Rank cross-sectionally, monthly.", "rationale": "A sharp recent surge in relative volume often reflects unsustainable attention and overpricing that subsequently reverses.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (recent volume below its longer-run norm)"}, {"name": "Book Leverage Change Quality", "construction": "Compute year-over-year change in the ratio of total debt (Compustat DLTT + DLC) to total assets (AT). Rank firms; those reducing leverage while maintaining or growing assets score highest. Lag 6 months.", "rationale": "Voluntary deleveraging signals management confidence and reduced financial risk that the market recognizes only gradually.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (declining book leverage)"}, {"name": "Gross-Margin Trend Stability", "construction": "Compute gross margin ((SALE - COGS)/SALE) for each of the past four fiscal years, then take the trailing four-year slope minus its standard deviation. High score means steadily rising, low-volatility margins. Lag 6 months.", "rationale": "Consistently expanding margins indicate widening competitive advantage that investors underweight relative to headline earnings.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (rising, stable gross margins)"}, {"name": "Idiosyncratic Return Skewness", "construction": "For each stock, regress daily excess returns on the market over the trailing 12 months and compute the skewness of the regression residuals. Rank cross-sectionally, monthly.", "rationale": "Investors overpay for lottery-like positive-skewness stocks, so negatively skewed idiosyncratic returns command a premium.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (negative idiosyncratic skewness)"}]}
